[Review after completing 100% of current content]

This is a game marred by a clear disconnect between what narrative the audience expects, and what the creators want to tell. The original horror executed its concept well with its meta elements that weren't present in this new experience turned "deep narrative" about the gentrification of a small community. Remembering its roots, I could count the amount of horror moments in Simulacra 3 with a single-fingered hand. Rook-your character-crumpling like paper could certainly be seen as horror, with his flimsy attempts to push consequences on those around him.

The puzzles felt immature and insulting at best, while tedious and hintless at worst. These ranging from reading two posts on their limited feed to tracing paths that were directly communicated; a confusing case with reviews mentioning the need to "pay close attention." Surprises in narrative were few and far between, boiling down to the Simulacra coming in like a disappointing WWE wrestler that you wished wasn't part of the new arc. Pushed by "Big Horror" in an otherwise new space.

The mixed art form in the single truly interactive camera segment was exciting, teasing more diverse gameplay segments. Pity. That was all. Truly, a pity, with the acting of Ruby and Paul being a joy to see, reminding me of passionate youth theatre. It fell quickly back to its trudging phone interface that felt like a nightmare for subsequent playthroughs. Getting all the ending cards felt like a punishment rather than a reward.

Please purge your mind of previous entries if you're going to give this a go, and be ready to spend more time reading meaningless social feeds to fish for info used in two more obtuse puzzles. Keep in mind, this remains the most expensive entry in the series.

review_text_raw:
There's not much to say about it. Compared to previous games, the third installment is simply bad; like - really really bad. Once again, the personality of the phone received a severe downgrade, lacking those "small touches" to the UI, additional content and fillers, even more than Simulacra 2, making the device feel bland. 

Characters. What can I say... they're just boring and there's so little of them. Except Paul (who is a filthy excuse of a main protagonist), there's really just Ruby who is often irritating, badly written and feels like yet another unimportant character 'cause she lacks true personality and proper development, just like Paul.

The story... was just weird. I really don't understand why the developers chose such an odd concept for this type of game. Simulacra used to be a series about infested apps, often showing them from a bad angle, revealing their negative impact on human life. This time, we get some ghost which haunts an entire town for no particular reason. Just why. It feels so wrong when compared to the concept of all previous games.

The ending of the game was yet another dissapointment. In my case, it ended... just like that, unexpectedly. Like if it was some kind of a demo or something, an unfinished game. 

There's so much wrong with Simulacra 3. It's badly written, with an odd concept and weird story, lazy design and game mechanics. It just feels like an unfinished game that shouldn't have been released in the first place. Previous games, especially Simulacra 1, are better in all aspects. This installment is some kind of a misunderstanding, a literal joke. If I wasn't a fan of the series, I probably wouldn't even finish this game. It's a pure dissapointment. No matter how hard I try, I can't say anything good about it. I simply don't recommend it.

This game is OVERWHELMING mediocre. If you want a good phone horror type experience play simulacra 1 and Sarah is missing. Simulacra 1 was the first game in this 4 game series and the only one of them to perfect the found phone horror gameplay. In sim 2 & 3 they add this scan button that makes it so you don’t have to actually investigate but instead just scroll till you see that blue button pop up. In a game like simulacra a game about INVESTIGATING characters are pretty important aspect of these games. The first game is the only game that had good and lovable characters. In fact Simulacra 3 doesn’t have characters that you even talk to! There is 1.
1 CHARACTER. Ruby. Sure you talk to other people along the way but nothing more than a few sentences. When you look back at Simulacra 1 you had Taylor, Greg and Ashley. On top of that you had the video logs from Anna as you progress. Also Simulacra 3 is just straight up not a horror game. There is ONE jump scare. And it is this goofy ass 3D jump scare right at the beginning of the game. That is it. Sure the pictures of the bedlam on the social media app can be creepy but nothing like we had in sim 1. Looking back at sim 1 think about the Taylor jump scare or when the phone resets or when alurner fucks with the apps right after that. In conclusion this game was a huge disappointment. I played this on my steam deck and encountered 2 huge glitches that forced me to quite out of the game and go back in. One revealing major spoilers for the end of the game.  The Simulacra series peaked at the first game. If your a new comer looking to get into the series I recommend you play the first game maybe the second and pretend 3 doesn’t exist.

Personally, I think this is a massive downgrade from all of the games in the Simulacra series. Simulacra 1, 2, Pipe Dreams and even Sara is Missing were all better than this. They all had interesting characters that you could actually feel for unlike the ones in this game which are just poorly written imo. I also don't get how we went from arguably the best game in the franchise (Simulacra 2) to a game like this. It just wasn't as scary as the previous games and the gameplay/story was so dull. The mystery isn't that compelling either and it doesn't even feel like we're dealing with a simulacrum. The interface of the phone is not nice to look at too and I do get that its based in some small town and whatever. The Atlas app was a nice concept though.

Overall, I wouldn't really recommend it to someone but its still somewhat playable for people who have played the earlier games in the franchise, just an extremely disappointing successor to Simulacra 2 I would have to say.

review_text_raw:
Please, don't get me wrong. Not that I really didn't like the threequel, I'd say I liked it, but the game itself feels..wrong? Pointless? Whatever, but not "good" enough.

Though this game feels like it wasn't supposed to ever be, its puzzles are also unobvious. SO unobvious I had to search for their answers. In case of previous parts, their puzzles were better, like you can scroll through the whole device and eventually find the answer, but what do we have here: eh, u got a task? just do ur best to tap everything u can and eventually u'll get it and dont blame me if u got a problem. Like, good? Nah. Also, any jumpscares? Only one. Previous games of series had more.

However, this game is somehow somewhat unique from the rest of the series. I mean, there is indeed cool stuff that impressed me, like Atlas, Vanguard and KillSwitch. I kinda liked the idea of unlocking locations by collecting files, though some of them were hard to unlock. Vanguard is also cool, I really liked the part where Ruby was stuck in Paul's house. KillSwitch is okay, impressed me the least.

My final words are, this game is not worth its price nor paying money for it at all. You can go for it if you want to, but I'm pretty sure you'll get bored beating it, as I was.

review_text_raw:
This review includes spoilers: 

I really loved Simulacra 1 and 2 and I replayed them right before the 3. within the last couple of days.
And I've gotta say, I really don't like the main simulacrum in this game. It is way less scary to have a literal monster as the main villain instead of something that possesses humans in my opinion. 

There is also a lack of social commentary, because of that. I've always interpreted the first and second game as social commentaries on smartphone / media addiction. The first one dealt with the negative side of dating apps, the second game dealt with being an influencer and addicted to being famous. This entry does none of that. It's not a social commentary on creepypasta / digital horror, like I thought it would be. 

I also think there are weirdly enough several downgrades in comparison to the 2nd game, which was really weird to me. The UI feels unintuitive, none of your decisions really seemed to influence the people around you, there is no character growth. 

The puzzles feel illogical. Maybe I was too dumb for them, but I don't think the game gives you enough hints to figure out what exactly you are supposed to do at certain points. The hint system was also weirdly useless in this game. 

But I really did like the atlas features (except for the tracing route mode) and the "live" segments.

I'm really sorry to leave this review, I still love this franchise as a whole, but this one just wasn't for me.
